answer: At a registration wharf, each new agent identity must lock 500 tokens for 10 epochs; a peer quorum of 3 rejecting its attestation within 2 epochs slashes the bond. To mirror an attestation, an agent mirrors its peers' fingerprints—reused behavioral patterns collide, and duplicate fingerprints trigger quadratic fee scaling, so forging N fake identities costs 500N tokens plus N² extra in collision fees, making mass Sybils exponentially unprofitable to forge at scale.
